summary: Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling (1973) and Tekchen Lekshay Ling (1988), and served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School (~1962) and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling (~1976).

Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.
Karsé Kongtrul studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Khakyab Dorje (~1904–1922). He taught Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunesh Shukla is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1991).

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz studied at the University of Bonn (PhD, Habilitation). A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, she was a professor (appointed 1999), faculty dean (2007–2010), and emerita (~2023) at the University of Bern.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal studied at the University of Allahabad, University of Oxford (Jesus College), and Lincoln's Inn. Working in Indology and history/archaeology, he was Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India (~1937).

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1944.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. In Indology, he held posts at Elphinstone College, served as syndic (1881) and vice-chancellor (1892–1893) of the University of Mumbai, and presided over the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1892–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and later as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1957).

Kate Crosby works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at Cardiff University, the Buddhist Institute (2003), SOAS University of London, and King's College London, where she is attested as Visiting Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Kate Kragh works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She is attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Kate Sullivan de Estrada works in Indology and international relations. As attested in 2026, she is an Associate Professor in the International Relations of South Asia at both Wolfson College, Oxford, and the University of Oxford.
Kate Wharton, a scholar of philosophy and Indology, completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London in 2008. She held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017. She has held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway studied religious studies and Buddhist studies at McGill University, earning a Master of Arts under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under Gudrun Bühnemann and was taught by Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at Davidson College and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.
Katherine K. Young studied at the University of Chicago and McGill University. Working in Indology and religious studies, she served as a professor at McGill University from ~1978 to 2016.
Katherine R. Tsiang is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who has held a faculty post at the University of Chicago (attested in 2012 and 2026).
